title: Shannon v. Shannon, S-25-546 (Neb. 2026)

reading.body:
This is not a record of an AI system failing in the world. It is a record of a document that could not be read. The only readable content is a Nebraska Supreme Court Online Library header, a web address, and a timestamp. Everything else is raw PDF file data, internal object references, font and page settings, and compressed streams.

The failure here is one of extraction, not of deployment. A court opinion PDF was ingested or linked in a form that yielded no case facts, no parties, no holdings and no numbers. Nothing in the given facts shows a model asserting something false, a system acting without human review, or an impersonation. What it shows is a pipeline that surfaced a file whose substantive content never became available.

Catching this would have required a check that the extracted text actually contains readable prose before the item was treated as a source. A length or character-class test on the output, or a human glance at the rendered page, would have flagged it. It is not established what the underlying case was about, who the parties were, or what the court decided, and the presence of a case citation is not a finding about any AI system.
